He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]] before going undrafted in the [[2003 NBA draft]]. He played his first three years for the [[Dallas Mavericks]] before being traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]]. Daniels then signed with the [[Boston Celtics]] in 2009 and the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in 2012. ==High school career== Daniels attended [[Edgewater High School]] in his hometown [[Orlando, Florida]], before transferring to [[Mt. Zion Christian Academy]] for his senior year.{{cite web |last=Kauffman |first=Scott |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/1998/12/10/former-edgewater-star-daniels-to-visit-with-new-teammates/ |title=Former Edgewater Star Daniels To Visit – With New Teammates |work=OrlandoSentinel.com |date=December 10, 1998 |access-date=August 12, 2014}} ==College career== In his four-year career at [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], Daniels played 111 games, averaging 13.8 points, 5.6 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.9 steals in 28.7 minutes per game.{{cite news|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/marquis-daniels-1.html |title=Marquis Daniels Stats |work=Sports-Reference.com |accessdate=August 12, 2014}} In 2003, Auburn reached the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|Sweet 16]] where Daniels averaged 23.3 points and 7.0 rebounds in three games, including an impressive 27-point, nine-rebound performance in a close one-point loss against the eventual national champion [[Syracuse University|Syracuse]].{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/scores103/103087/20030328NCAABSYRACUSE--0nr.htm |title=Auburn vs. Syracuse |work=USAToday.com |date=March 28, 2003 |accessdate=August 12, 2014}} Daniels graduated from [[Auburn University]] with a [[Academic degree|degree]] in [[Sociology]] in just three-and-a-half years. He averaged 18.4 points, 6.2 [[rebound (sports term)|rebound]]s, 3.3 [[assist (basketball)|assist]]s and 2.3 steals per game as a senior, and was named to the All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] second team as a senior and team [[Most Valuable Player|MVP]] as a sophomore, junior and senior. ==Professional career== ===Dallas Mavericks (2003–2006)=== After going undrafted in the [[2003 NBA draft]], Daniels joined the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for the 2003 [[NBA Summer League]] and later signed a one-year deal with the Mavericks. Daniels was mostly a third-stringer during his rookie season, used only when victory was all but sure. In the short minutes he was on the floor however, he showed flashes of brilliance. When [[Steve Nash]] was out with a stomach flu, head coach [[Don Nelson]] plugged in Daniels as the starting point guard and the rookie delivered with a near triple-double finishing with 14 points, 9 rebounds and 9 assists followed by a 16-point, 7 rebound and 8 assist game.{{cite web |title=SuperSonics vs Mavericks, March 2, 2004 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/200403020DAL.html |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=November 13, 2024}}{{cite web |title=Mavericks vs Timberwolves, March 3, 2004 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/200403030MIN.html |website=Basketball Reference |access-date=November 13, 2024}} Although his time as a starter was short, after the team played struggled with Daniels out of the starting line-up decided to bring him back and put him back in the classic ''small ball'' line-up in a 118–88 triumph over the [[Orlando Magic]] on March 28, 2004.{{cite web |title=Mavericks vs Magic, March 28, 2004 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/200403280ORL.html |website=Basketball Reference |access-date=November 13, 2004}} This line-up had the 6'9" [[Antoine Walker]] at [[Center (basketball)|center]] and Daniels at shooting guard, and was the permanent starting five member until their premature post-season demise. Daniels averaged 19.7 points, 6 rebounds and 5 assists during that 10-game stretch. In July 2004, Daniels re-joined the Mavericks for the 2004 NBA Summer League and later signed a six-year, $38 million contract with the Mavericks.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=1833400 |title=Daniels gets six-year deal; Harris signs |publisher=ESPN |date=July 2, 2004 |access-date=August 12, 2014}} ===Indiana Pacers (2006–2009)=== On July 12, 2006, Daniels was traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in exchange for [[Austin Croshere]].{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/croshere-daniels-071206.shtml |title=Mavs trade Marquis Daniels to Pacers for Austin Croshere |work=InsideHoops.com |date=July 12, 2006 |accessdate=August 12, 2014}} On June 30, 2009, the Pacers announced their decision to not exercise their team option on the final year of Daniels' six-year contract, making him an unrestricted free agent.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4294765 |title=Pacers won't pick up Daniels' option |publisher=ESPN |date=June 30, 2009 |access-date=August 12, 2014}} ===Boston Celtics (2009–2012)=== On September 1, 2009, Daniels signed with [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4438279 |title=Celtics sign former Pacer Daniels |publisher=ESPN |date=September 1, 2009 |access-date=August 12, 2014}} On February 6, 2011, while the Celtics were playing against the [[Orlando Magic]], Daniels collided with Magic guard [[Gilbert Arenas]] and suffered a bruised spinal cord. Daniels laid motionless on the floor for several minutes before being taken away on a stretcher. He gave the Boston crowd a thumbs up sign, and after arriving at a Boston Hospital, regained movement of his arms and legs.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nba/news/story?id=6095978 |title=Marquis Daniels has bruised spine |publisher=ESPN |date=February 7, 2011 |access-date=August 12, 2014}} On February 24, 2011, Daniels was traded, along with cash considerations, to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in exchange for a 2017 protected second-round draft pick.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/press_release_2011_02_24.html |title=Kings Acquire Marquis Daniels |work=NBA.com |date=February 24, 2011 |accessdate=August 12, 2014}} On July 1, 2011, he became a free agent, departing the Kings before playing in a game for them. On December 9, 2011, Daniels re-signed with the Boston Celtics on a one-year deal.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/press120911-celtics-sign-daniels.html |title=Celtics Sign Marquis Daniels |work=NBA.com |date=December 9, 2011 |accessdate=August 12, 2014}} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2012–2013)=== On September 25, 2012, Daniels signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-marquis-daniels |title=Bucks Sign Marquis Daniels |work=NBA.com |date=September 25, 2012 |accessdate=August 12, 2014}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 111 || 90 || 28.7 || .496 || .296 || .646 || 5.6 || 2.6 || 1.9 || .4 || 13.8 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== ===Tattoos=== Daniels is noted for having several tattoos inscribed on different parts of his body. The tattoos range from a detailed map of Florida that covers his entire back, a caricature of a man blowing his head off with a [[shotgun]] on his lower right arm, and Chinese characters on his other arm which were intended to represent his initials, but translate to English as "healthy woman roof". Also, he has an entire Bible verse on his chest, which he used to read to his paralyzed grandmother.{{cite web |url=http://tattoomagz.com/marquis-daniels-tattoo/marquis-daniels-youritlist/ |title=ALL MARQUIS DANIELS TATTOOS |work=TattooMagz.com |accessdate=August 12, 2014}} ===Rap career=== Outside basketball, Daniels also has a career in the hip-hop industry, going by his stage name, "Q6".{{cite web |last=Shropshire |first=Terry |url=http://rollingout.com/music/nba-baller-marquis-daniels-powers-his-way-to-rap-respectability/ |title=NBA Player Marquis Daniels Powers His Way to Rap Respectability |work=RollingOut.com |date=September 28, 2012 |accessdate=August 12, 2014}} One of his top singles is "Kome Here Nikki".{{cite web |title=Kome Here Nikki |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ASgxXy2EuCs |website=Youtube |access-date=November 13, 2024}} Daniels has collaborated with many artists including Torrence "[[Lil Boosie]]" Hatch, [[Gucci Mane]],{{cite web |last1=Mane |first1=Gucci |title=Pussy & Patron |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DTiZSo48taA |website=Youtube |access-date=November 13, 2024}} and {{cite web |last1=Acosta |first1=David |title=An Interview with the Boston Celtics' Marquis Daniels |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/433119-an-interview-w-marquis-daniels |website=Bleacher Report |access-date=November 13, 2024}} [[Trina]]. ===Coaching career=== In retirement, Daniels has also begun to coach. He is currently serving as an assistant men's basketball coach at his alma mater, [[Auburn University]].{{cite web |title=Marquis Daniels |url=https://auburntigers.com/staff/marquis-daniels |website=Auburn Tigers |access-date=November 13, 2024}} ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== *[http://stats.nba.com/playerProfile.html?PlayerID=2605 NBA.com profile] *{{basketballstats|bbr=d/daniema01}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Daniels, Marquis}} [[Category:1981 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Auburn Tigers men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Orlando, Florida]] [[Category:Boston Celtics players]] [[Category:Dallas Mavericks players]] [[Category:Indiana Pacers players]] [[Category:Milwaukee Bucks players]] [[Category:People from Jasper, Florida]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Edgewater High School alumni]] [[Category:Parade High School All-Americans (boys' basketball)]] [[Category:Small forwards]] [[Category:Undrafted NBA players]]
